Subject: Questionnaires - data residency & deletion (hosted API)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our standard security questionnaire — the sections we care most about right now are data residency, retention windows, and deletion/erasures for your hosted API. A few specific asks:

1) Where is customer content stored/processed by default?  Do you offer region selection (US/EU/APAC)?
2) What are default retention windows for prompts, generations, embeddings, and logs?
3) How does deletion work (immediate delete vs background GC vs backups)? Typical SLA we expect: confirmation of deletion event + audit stamp.
4) Do you ever use customer content to train models? If not, how is that controlled and reflected in the DPA?
5) What is your backup/snapshot retention and how quickly can backups be purged on request?

If you can reply with short, point-form responses and any relevant attachments (redacted examples are fine) that would help our procurement/security review.

Best,
Samantha

Sr. Security PM — XenoTech

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending this over. Answers below (short, numbered to match your questions). I’ve attached a CSV that maps object types to default retention and a small redacted audit-log sample for reference. Happy to expand any of these.

1) Data residency and processing
- Default: customer content for hosted API accounts provisioned in our US region (us-central).
- Region selection: we offer US and EU regions for hosted tenancy; APAC options are available on request (enterprise/private deployments). Region is selectable at account creation or via Console for new resource groups.
- Data in transit and at rest is encrypted (TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 using customer or provider KMS for at-rest).

2) Default retention windows (live stores) — redwood-hosted defaults (customer-configurable TTLs):
- Prompts & model inputs: 30 days (default).
- Generated outputs (tokens): 30 days (default).
- Embeddings & vector indexes: 90 days by default, configurable per-index.
- Operational logs (API request metadata, telemetry): 90 days by default; PII is redacted on ingest where possible.
- KV cache (short-term inference cache): ephemeral, typically 0–24 hours depending on workload and batching configuration; not used for long-term storage.

3) Deletion process and evidence
- Customer-initiated deletion: open a request via our support portal (link below) with account id and object identifiers.
- Immediate visible deletion: once a deletion request is acknowledged, objects are removed from live primary stores within 0–72 hours (most deletes are completed <24h).
- Backups & snapshots: default backup retention is 30 days; backups are immutable snapshots stored encrypted. Deleting an object triggers background GC that flags snapshots for purge; purging backups can take up to 30 days unless an expedited purge is contracted.
- Audit evidence: we provide a deletion confirmation email and an audit event id; for customers on Dedicated/Private or bespoke contracts we can provide a signed attestation and access to audit logs.

4) Model training & data use
- Hosted API: customer content is NOT used for training or improving model weights by default. We have an explicit opt-in for any program that would use customer data for research/training; this is also stated in our DPA.

5) Backups, snapshots, and expedited purge
- Default: backups retained 30 days.
- Expedited purge: available for enterprise customers with SLA & DPA clauses (time-to-purge varies with scope; typical accelerated windows are 7–14 days after contractual amendment).

Next steps / attachments
- Attached: redwood-hostedapi-data-retention-table.csv (maps data types -> default TTL -> configurable) and sample-audit-logs.txt (redacted).
- Support ticket link to trigger an erasure: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/123456 (include account id + object identifiers).

If you want, I can loop in Neha (security/compliance) or Karthik (infra) for a short call to walk through backup purge options and DPA language.

Best,

Jordan — thanks, that’s helpful. A couple of follow-ups after looking at the CSV and sample logs:

- For backups: you said backups are immutable snapshots. If we request an erasure for a user account and the object appears in a snapshot, do you create a new snapshot that excludes the object (and then GC the older one), or do you mark the snapshot and wait for the 30-day window? In short: can we get a contractual guarantee that objects will be fully purged from all backup/snapshot copies within X days?

- Logs: your sample shows request_id and partial payloads. We need to confirm whether logs ever contain full PII (phone/email) and if so, whether you can purge or suppress those log records tied to deletion requests.

- Region: if we select EU for a tenant, are backups and processing guaranteed to remain in-region (no cross-border replication)?

We’d like a short paragraph per bullet that we can insert into our security review doc. Also please confirm whether the deletion confirmation includes an audit event id we can reference in our SOC2 evidence.

Thanks — Samantha

On behalf of XenoTech security

Hi Samantha — looping in the infra & compliance details below (short, bullet answers you can paste into your doc). Jordan, please send these as the formal reply to Samantha and offer a 30-minute call if they want escalation.

- Backups/snapshots and purging:
  • We do not edit immutable snapshots in-place. When a deletion request is received we mark the object as deleted in the primary live store and create a tombstone that prevents rehydration into new snapshots.
  • Existing immutable snapshots are flagged for GC; by default snapshots are purged in up to 30 days.
  • For contractual expedited purge: we can commit to a 14-day purge window for hosted API under an SLA addendum (work with legal to add DPA clause). Expedited purges require an ops runbook and may require temporary read-only access from SRE to confirm deletion events.

- Logs and PII:
  • We redact known PII on ingest for telemetry. However, request payloads may contain customer-supplied data; we treat those as customer content.
  • On erasure requests we will locate associated log records (by request_id, account id) and redact or remove full payloads where feasible. We provide an audit event id for the erasure and a summary of records altered.

- Regional guarantees:
  • For EU-region tenants we provision primary and backup storage within EU regions and do not replicate to US regions by default. Cross-border replication only occurs for customers who opt into multi-region replication.

- Audit evidence & SOC2:
  • Deletion confirmation includes an audit event id and timestamp. For customers requiring enhanced evidence we can deliver a signed attestation and provide access to an S3-compatible audit export for the event range (per contract).

Jordan — suggested reply: short paragraph bullets answering Samantha’s three bullets + offer an ops call and attach the CSV + sample logs (redacted). Happy to join the call if they want technical detail.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
